title: Roomlight is out: baked lighting for the rooms your Unity 6 game spawns
body:
Roomlight is out: baked lighting for the rooms your Unity 6 game spawns.

Unity stores baked lighting per scene, so a room built as a prefab and spawned at runtime (a looping hallway, a dungeon room, a pooled level chunk) arrives with no lightmap and is lit only by its lights in real time. Roomlight bakes each room prefab alone with Unity's own lightmapper, copies the pages beside the prefab, and writes a component that binds every spawned copy to them. Copies of one room share one set of pages.

What we measured before shipping:

  • Each of the three demo rooms was baked by Roomlight itself, alone, with Unity's lightmapper in batch mode: 2, 2, 2 pages, 7, 7, 8 renderers and 2, 2, 2 baked lights, 34 to 38 seconds a room.
  • 9 spawned copies of the three rooms, all bound: 9 of 9, sharing 6 lightmap slots (3 rooms, two pages each), not 18.
  • In a real Windows player build of the demo, all 66 of 66 spawned renderers read their room's bake. Mean brightness of the same view: 78.9 with Roomlight, 48.5 with the rooms' lights in real time.
  • The same build with Lightmap Modes left on Automatic: 23.9, darker than real time, because the lightmap shaders were stripped. Roomlight's build check stopped that build before it was made; Auto-fix on build made it safe and the build succeeded.
  • Installed from the shipped .unitypackage into a blank project with no graphics device: 13 of 14 tests passed, 0 failed (one thumbnail test needs a GPU), and the rooms baked headless.

The part we did not expect to matter as much: on Lightmap Modes = Automatic, Unity keeps only the lightmap shaders the scenes in the build use. Spawn baked rooms into a scene with no baked light of its own and the player build strips them, so the rooms render darker than plain real time while looking right in the Editor. Roomlight's build check stops that build and names the one click that fixes it.

Tested on 6000.5.7f1 with the Built-in Render Pipeline; URP, HDRP and Mixed lights were not tested for this version, and the listing says so.

Roomlight on itch.io, $9.99, full C# source, a numbered guide and a demo scene.
